messages:
alex: Quick sync — we still have divergent auth/secret flows between hosted/dedicated/private. Need a decision before next week's rollout. High-level options: 1) Control-plane translate tokens + keep secret blind to runtime; 2) Push full credential ownership to runtime adapters (sidecar/HSM). Which do we pick?

sophia: I'd vote control-plane translate for hosted/dedicated; private customers often require on-prem HSM so they need option (2). Main risk: control-plane can't access HSM-wrapped keys.

kevin: Tradeoff: compliance/audit visibility vs operational complexity and secret surface. If we translate tokens we must issue short-lived mTLS certs + scope mapping + rotation automation.

matt: We should formalize a capability manifest that runtimes advertise. Control-plane makes decision per-request.

matt: ```json
{"capabilities": ["aws-kms","hsm","no-external-egress"], "auth_flow": "translate-or-delegate", "probe_endpoint": "/v1/probe"}
```

priya: Telemetry requirement: tag every request with `authz_mode` (translate|delegate) and `capability_hash` so we can attribute cost/regressions.

kevin: Fallback semantics question — if runtime reports lacking capability, do we fallback to hosted-serving? For private tenants that would be data egress — I'd vote fail-closed by default and require explicit allowlist for fallback via customer opt-in.

matt: Migration plan proposal: 1) Build capability registry + probe, 2) Deploy probe across runtime fleet (nonblocking), 3) Canary flow that uses translated tokens for a small % of requests, 4) Increase scope, 5) Flip default for non-sensitive tenants.

alex: Action items: matt to draft capability schema RFC, kevin to write failover policy (fail-closed default; explicit allowlist for fallback), priya to define telemetry keys and span attributes, sophia to coordinate legal on allowed fallback list for private customers. I'll own the rollout checklist. If anyone wants to push back, say so by EOD Friday.

sophia: I'll loop in legal and security. Note: Dedicated customers currently using sidecar model — ensure adapter backwards compatibility (adapter shim) or provide migration script.

kevin: One more operational caveat: token-translate requires a short-lived signing service. We should plan for rate-limited signing and an emergency manual key rotation procedure.

priya: Also add a metric `auth_translation_error_rate` and an alert SLO so we can catch regressions quickly.

deploy-bot: Reminder: adapter-probe service scheduled deploy 2026-04-01T03:00:00Z to staging :rocket:

alex: thanks all. If no objections we'll proceed with control-plane translate + capability manifest + strict fail-closed for private tenants. Will put RFC draft in #architecture/rfcs.

kevin: +1 :thumbsup:

matt: +1

priya: +1

sophia: +1 — will start legal thread.
